name: Low-Sodium Hospital Diet (2 g sodium)
description: Restricts sodium to 2,000 mg/day, distributed across meals, while guarding against under-eating on a restricted diet.
disclaimer: Thresholds are illustrative and codified from public guidance. Verify against your institution's approved diet manual before clinical use.

rules.title: Daily sodium limit

evidence.source: WHO Guideline: Sodium intake for adults and children (2012)
evidence.note: Adults should consume less than 2 g sodium per day.

rules.remedy: Replace high-sodium items with fresh or no-salt-added alternatives; remove added salt.

rules.title: Main meal sodium cap

evidence.source: Common institutional practice for 2 g Na diets
evidence.note: Spreading sodium roughly evenly (about 600-700 mg per main meal) keeps the daily total achievable.

rules.remedy: Rebalance sodium across meals so no single meal consumes most of the daily allowance.

rules.title: Snack sodium cap

evidence.source: Common institutional practice for 2 g Na diets
evidence.note: Snacks are typically allotted a small share of the daily sodium budget.

rules.remedy: Choose unsalted snacks such as fresh fruit or unsalted nuts.

rules.title: Prohibited high-sodium foods

evidence.note: Processed and cured foods, canned soups and salty snacks are major sodium sources.

rules.remedy: Swap for fresh, unprocessed or no-salt-added versions.

rules.title: Minimum meal frequency

evidence.note: Restricted diets raise the risk of inadequate intake; at least three eating occasions are expected.

rules.remedy: Add a meal or snack to the day.

rules.title: Minimum energy intake (adequacy)

evidence.note: Diet restrictions should not result in inadequate energy intake.

rules.remedy: Increase portions or add compliant, energy-dense foods.
